meaning.evidence: The normalized direction is the stress divided by its length, the unit vector pointing in the same direction, and it extends from the open annulus to the closed collars.

notation.evidence: The domain is X_a<X<X_b, and Theorem 4.6(iii) supplies the positive margin on the closed collars.

prerequisites.evidence: The stress is flat at both edges, nonzero on the open annulus, and has a stated positive-margin extension.

proof_job.evidence: The direction is the quantity whose edge limits and cone margin must be controlled by the later construction.

target.exact_quote:
The stress will be flat at both edges. Wherever the stress is nonzero, its normalized direction is
found by dividing the stress by its length, so it is the unit vector that points in the same direction
as the stress. The theorem below states that the constructed stress is nonzero on the marked open
annulus \NSi{NS-F-P032-030}{X_a<X<X_b}, so its normalized direction is defined there. It also
extends that direction to the closed collars with the positive margin stated in
Theorem~\ref{thm:4.6}(iii). The construction results used in that proof come after the theorem.

The construction results used in the proof are stated after the theorem.

meaning.evidence: After a regular inner extension has the same moments, stress can be computed by integrating backward from infinity instead of outward from the axis.

notation.evidence: No new formula symbol appears in this sentence; the direction and endpoint of integration are stated in words.

prerequisites.evidence: The heat exterior, outward axis formula, matching moments, and regular inner extension are all named before the backward integral is used.

proof_job.evidence: The backward representation supplies the outer-edge conclusions and makes the limiting stress direction explicit.

target.exact_quote:
The exterior is now prepared with the right moments and heat flow. Its stress
was defined by integrating outward from the axis. To get the conclusions at
the outer edge as well, it still needs a regular inner extension with the
same moments. Once that condition is met, the stress can instead be
integrated backward from infinity, and its limiting direction can be found
explicitly.

source_locator.exact_text: The prepared exterior has the correct moments and heat flow. Its stress is defined by integration from the axis, so the outer edge conclusions also require a regular inner extension with the same moments. Under that condition, the stress can be integrated from infinity and its limiting direction can be determined explicitly.
